So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I went out and sat by the pulpit and then I was overcome by what I felt. So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I turned away and the slave called me and said: Come in, you have been given permission. So I entered and greeted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there he was. Leaning on the sand of a mat - Imam Ahmad said: And Yaqub narrated to us in the hadith of Salih, who said: The sand of a mat - and it left an impression on his side, so I said: O Messenger of God, have you divorced your wives? He raised his head to me and said: No. So I said: God is Great. And if you had seen us, O Messenger of God, we Quraysh were a people who would overpower women, but when we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women overpowered them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day, my wife became angry with me, and I found her arguing with me, so I disapproved of her arguing with me. She said: Why do you disapprove of my arguing with you? By God, the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arguing with him, and one of them would ignore him from day to night. So I said: He who does that among you has failed and lost. Does any of you feel secure that God will not be angry with her because of the anger of the Messenger of God, and then she will be ruined? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) smiled, so I said: O Messenger of God, I entered upon Hafsa and said: Do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful or more beloved to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than you. He smiled again, so I said: Be comforted, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes. So I sat and raised my head in the house, and by God, I did not see anything in the house that would delight the eye except the preparations for his position. I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant your nation more abundantly, for He granted the Persians and Romans more abundantly, yet they did not worship God. He sat up straight and said: Are you in doubt, O son of Al-Khattab? They are a people for whom their good things have been hastened in the life of this world. I said: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month because of the intensity of his resentment towards them, until God, the Almighty, admonished him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id Al-Ansari on the authority of Ubayd ibn Hunayn on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I spent a year wanting to ask Umar ibn Al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not ask him out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj, so I went out with him. When we returned, and we were partway through the Hajj, he turned towards the arak tree because of some need he had. I stood until he finished, then I walked with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women who conspired against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. Muslim narrated it: Who are the two women about whom God the Most High said: And if they both conspire against him? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. Then he narrated the hadith in full, and some of them abbreviated it. Muslim also said: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Umar bin Yunus al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, on the authority of Samak bin al-Walid Abu Zamil, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin al-Khattab told me, he said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque, and I saw the people poking stones and saying, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had divorced his wives.” That was before the veil was ordered, so I said, I will know that today. Then he mentioned the hadith about his entering upon Aisha and Hafsa and advising them, until he said: So I entered and saw Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the threshold of the window. So I called out and said, “O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, until he said, “So I said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is difficult for you regarding the matter of women? If you have divorced them, then God is with you, and His angels, Gabriel, Michael, Abu Bakr, and I, and the believers, and I rarely spoke—and I praise God—with anything except that I hoped that it would be…’” God confirms my words, so this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you all, will give him in exchange wives better than you “And if they both back him up against him - indeed, God is his Protector and [so will] Gabriel and the righteous believers and the angels after that as support.” So I said: Have you divorced them? He said: No. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: He has not divorced his wives. And this verse was revealed: “And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, then those who can investigate it would have known about it.” So I was the one who investigated that information. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ad-Dahhak and others said: And the righteous believers means Abu Bakr and Umar. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Uthman added. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said on the authority of Mujahid: And the righteous believers means Ali bin Abi Talib. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Abi Omar told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: A trustworthy man told me, tracing it back to Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God the Most High: And the righteous believers, he said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib. Its chain of transmission is weak and it is very objectionable. Al-Bukhari said: Umar bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, he said: Umar said: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered in jealousy for him, so I said to them: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. So this verse was revealed. It was mentioned before that it coincided with the Qur’an in several places: one of them in the revelation of the veil, one of them in the case of the captives of Badr, and one of them in His statement: If you took the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. So God the Most High revealed: And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Ansari told us, Humayd told us, on the authority of Anas, he said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: I was informed of something that happened between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I settled them down saying: Either you refrain from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or God will replace him with wives better than you, until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers and she said: O Umar, is there not in the Messenger of God enough to admonish his wives so that you admonish them? So I held back and God the Almighty revealed: Perhaps if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in exchange wives better than you - Muslims, believers, obedient, repentant, worshipping God, fasting, married and virgins. This woman who turned him away from what he was doing of admonishing women was Umm Salamah as proven in Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim bin Nailah Al-Asbahani narrated to us, Ismail Al-Bajali narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement: And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, he said: Hafsah entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in her house while he was having intercourse with Maria. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her: “Do not tell Aisha until I give you good report: your father will succeed Abu Bakr when I die.” So Hafsah went and informed Aisha, and Aisha said to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: Who told you this? He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me. Aisha said: I will not look at you until you forbid Maria. So he forbade her, and then God, the Most High, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid [her]? Its chain of transmission is questionable. The interpretation of these noble verses has become clear from what we have mentioned, and the meaning of His statement: Muslim women, believing women, obedient, repentant, worshipping is clear. God the Almighty says: Travelers meaning: fasting. This was said by Abu Hurairah, Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, Abu Malik, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Suddi and others. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was presented in Surat Al-Bara’ah, in which the wording is: The traveler of this nation is fasting. Zayd bin Aslam and his son Abd Al-Rahman said: Travelers meaning emigrants. Abd Al-Rahman recited: Travelers, meaning emigrants. The first statement is better, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Women who are married and virgins meaning that some of them are married and some of them are virgins so that this would be more desirable to the soul, because variety expands the soul, and for this reason He said: Women who are married and virgins. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his great dictionary: Abu Bakr ibn Sadaqa told us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq told us, Abdullah ibn Umayya told us, Abdul Quddus told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, Women who are married and virgins he said: God promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse that He would marry him, so the married woman is Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and the virgins are Mary, the daughter of Imran. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Mary, peace be upon her, on the authority of Suwaid bin Saeed: Muhammad bin Salih bin Umar told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Khadija passed by. He said: God sends her greetings and gives her good tidings of a house in Paradise made of hollow pearls, far from play, in which there is no toil or noise. From the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Khadijah while she was dying and said: O Khadijah, when you meet your co-wives, greet them from me. She said: “O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did you marry before me?” He said: No, but God married me to Mary, the daughter of Imran, Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Kulthum, the sister of Moses. This is also weak. Abu Ya’la said: Ibrahim ibn Arara told us, Abd al-Nur ibn Abdullah told us, Yusuf ibn Shu’ayb told us, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you know that God married me in Paradise to Mary, the daughter of Imran, Kulthum, the sister of Moses, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh? I said: Congratulations, O Messenger of God. This is also weak and was narrated as a mursal hadith on the authority of Ibn Abi Dawud.
66:4: There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of the beginning of this Surah. It has been said that it was revealed concerning Maria, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had forbidden her. Then the words of God Almighty were revealed: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad told us, my father told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a female slave whom he would have intercourse with. Aisha and Hafsa kept at him until he forbade her. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? to the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan told us, Zayd ibn Aslam told me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had intercourse with the mother of Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: O Messenger of God, in my house and on my bed? So he made her forbidden to him. She said: O Messenger of God, how do you forbid yourself what is lawful? So he swore to her by God that he would not have intercourse with her. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? Zayd ibn Aslam said: His saying, You are forbidden to me, is meaningless. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated this on the authority of his father. Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: He said to her: You are forbidden to me, by God I will not have intercourse with you. Sufyan al-Thawri and Ibn Ulayyah said, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath and forbade it, so he was rebuked for forbidding it and was ordered to make expiation for the oath. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and it was also narrated on the authority of Qatada and others on the authority of al-Sha’bi himself, and more than one of the early Muslims said the same, including al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-Awfi narrated a long story on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya told us, my father told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Umar bin Al-Khattab: Who are the two women? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. The conversation began with the matter of Umm Ibrahim, Maria the Copt, whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had intercourse with in Hafsa’s house during her turn. Hafsa found him and said: O Prophet of God, you have done something to me that you have not done to any of your husbands on my day, in my turn, or on my bed. He said: Are you not pleased that I forbid her and do not approach her? She said: Yes. So he forbade her and said to her: Do not mention that to anyone. She mentioned it to Aisha, and God revealed it to him, and then God revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? and all the verses. It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) atoned for his oath and had intercourse with his slave girl. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb said in his Musnad: Abu Qilabah Abdul-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hafsah: Do not tell anyone, for the mother of Ibrahim is forbidden to me. She said: Do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: By God, I will not go near her. He said: So he did not go near her until she told Aishah. He said: Then God, the Most High, revealed: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. This is a saheeh chain of narration, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi chose it in his book al-Mustakhraj. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Hisham al-Dastawai told us: Yahya wrote to me, narrating on the authority of Ya’la bin Hakeem, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, that Ibn Abbas used to say that there is an oath that must be expiated for something forbidden. Ibn Abbas said, There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern, meaning that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl, so God, the Most High, said, “O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths.” So he expiated his oath, so the forbidden oath became an oath. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Mu’adh bin Fadalah, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai, on the authority of Yahya, who is Ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibn Hakeem, who is Ya’la, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the oath that must be expiated for something forbidden. Ibn Abbas said, There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern, and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai with it. Al-Nasa’i said: Abdullah bin Abdul Samad bin Ali informed us, Mukhallad - who is Ibn Yazid - told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said, I have made my wife forbidden to me. He said, You have lied; she is not forbidden to you. Then he recited this verse: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? The most severe expiation for you is the freeing of a slave. Al-Nasa’i is the only one who transmitted it from this source with this wording. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Zakariya told us, Abdullah bin Raja told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his concubine. From here, some of the jurists who said that expiation is obligatory for whoever forbids his concubine or wife, or food, drink, clothing, or any of the permissible things went, and this is the view of Imam Ahmad and a group. Al-Shafi’i said that expiation is not obligatory for anything other than the wife and the concubine if he forbade them specifically or made the prohibition general for them in one opinion. However, if he intended by the prohibition to divorce the wife or free the female slave, then it is valid for them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, Ikrimah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you? was revealed about the woman who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a strange statement, but the correct view is that it was regarding his prohibition of honey, as Al-Bukhari said regarding this verse: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to drink honey at the home of Zaynab bint Jahsh and stay with her. Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us he entered upon should say to him: I ate maghāfir, I smell the odor of maghāfir on you. He said: No, but I used to drink honey at the home of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not do it again, and I have sworn not to tell anyone about that, “seeking to please your wives.” This is how this hadith is mentioned here with this wording. He said in the Book of Oaths and Vows: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ claimed that he heard Ubayd bin Umair say: I heard Aisha claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey at her place. Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon should say to him, “I smell the odor of maghāfir on you. I have eaten maghāfir.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon one of them, and she said that to him. He said, No, but I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not do it again. Then the verse was revealed: “O Prophet! Why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. And God is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, then when she disclosed it and God disclosed it to him, he recognized part of it and turned away from part. But when he disclosed it to her, she said, ‘Who informed you of this?’ He said, ‘The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me. If you both repent to God, I will turn to You.’” God has made your hearts inclined” to Aisha and Hafsa And when the Prophet confided in some of his wives a matter to say: Rather, I drank honey. Ibrahim bin Musa said on the authority of Hisham: And I will not return to it, and I have sworn not to tell anyone about that. And thus he narrated it in the Book of Divorce with this chain of transmission and its wording is close to it, then he said: Al-Maghāfir is similar to gum that is found in the rimth and has sweetness, I forgive it with the rimth if it appears in it, its singular is maghūr and it is said maghāfir, and thus al-Jawhari said. He said that al-Maghfūr may also refer to the tenth, the thamām, the salm and the talh. He said that the rimth with a kasra is a pasture of camel pastures and it is from the sour. He said that the urfat is a tree from the tamarisk from which the maghūr exudes. Muslim narrated this hadith in the Book of Divorce in his Sahih on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatim on the authority of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who told me on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair on the authority of Aisha, and its wording is as Al-Bukhari included it in Oaths and Vows. Then Al-Bukhari said in the Book of al-Talaq 65:Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra’ told us, Ali ibn Masahr told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved sweets and honey, and when he finished the afternoon prayer, he would go to his wives and approach one of them. He went to Hafsah bint Umar and stayed longer than he usually stayed. I became jealous and asked about that, and it was said to me that a woman from her people had given her a gift of a bowl of honey, so she gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a drink of it. I said: By God, we will find a plan for him. I said to Sawdah bint Zam’ah: He will come close to you, and when he comes close to you, say, Did you eat some saffron? He will say, No. Then say to him, What is this smell that I smell? He will say, You gave me some. Hafsa gave me a drink of honey, so say, The bees of the thorn nectar have nibbled on it, and I will tell you. You tell him, Safiyya, that. She said, "Sawda says that. By God, he had just stood at the door, and I wanted to call him as you ordered me out of fear of you. But when he came close to her, Sawda said to him, "O Messenger of God, have you eaten maghāfir? He said, No. She said, What is this odor that I smell from you? He said, Hafsa gave me a drink of honey. She said, The bees of the thorn nectar have nibbled on it." When he came to me, I said something similar. When he came to Safiyya, she said the same to him. When he came to Hafsa, she said to him, "O Messenger of God, shall I not give you some to drink? He said, I have no need of it. Sawda said, By God, we have forbidden it. I said to her, Be quiet." This is the wording of Bukhari. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Suwaid bin Saeed, on the authority of Ali bin Masaher, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, Harun bin Abdullah, and Al-Hasan bin Bishr, all three of them on the authority of Abu Usamah Hammad bin Usamah, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, and with him she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be hard pressed to have a bad odor, meaning a foul odor, and for this reason they said to him, You ate Maghafir, because its odor has something to do with it. So when he said, Rather, you drank honey, they said, His bees grazed the Arfat tree, whose gum is Maghafir, and for this reason its odor appeared in the honey they drank. Al-Jawhari said: The bees grazed the Arfat tree, meaning they ate it, and from this the bees are called Jawaris. The poet said: *They remain on the fruits of it* Al-Jaras said: Al-Jaras is a low sound. It is said: I heard the bell of a bird if you heard the sound of its beaks on something it is eating. In the hadith: They hear the bell of the bird of Paradise. Al-Asma’i said: I was in Shu’bah’s assembly. He said: They hear the crunch of the bird of Paradise with the letter sh, so I said bell. He looked at me and said: Take it from him, for he knows this better than us. The point is that this context indicates that Hafsa was the one who brought the honey. It is from Hisham bin Urwa, from his father, from his aunt Aisha. In the chain of narration of Ibn Jurayj, from Ata’, from Ubaid bin Umair, from Aisha, that Zainab bint Jahsh was the one who brought him the honey, and that Aisha and Hafsa conspired and conspired against him. And God knows best. It may be said that they both occurred, and there is nothing wrong with that, except that their being a reason for the revelation of this verse is questionable, and God knows best. What indicates that Aisha and Hafsa may God be pleased with them are the two who supported each other is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I was always keen to ask Umar about the two women from the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about whom God the Most High said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined, until Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. When we were on the way, Umar turned aside and I turned aside with him with the water skin, so he defecated. Then he came to me and I poured water over his hands, and he performed ablution. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women from the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about whom God the Most High said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined, so Umar said: How strange you are, Ibn Abbas! Al-Zuhri said: By God, he disliked what he asked him about and did not conceal it. He said: They are Aisha and Hafsa. He said: Then he started to narrate the hadith. He said: We, the Quraysh, were a people who used to overpower women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women used to overpower them, so our women began to learn from their women. He said: My house was in the house of Umayyah ibn Zayd in Al-Awali. He said: One day I became angry with my wife, and she spoke to me in a rude tone. I disapproved of her speaking to me, so she said: Why do you disapprove of my speaking to you? By God, the wives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would speak to him in a rude tone, and one of them would ignore him from day to night. He said: So I went and entered upon Hafsa and said: Do you speak to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a rude tone? She said: Yes. I said: And one of you would ignore him from day to night? She said: Yes. I said: He among you who did that has failed and lost. Is any of you certain that God will not be angry with her because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed? Do not go back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not ask him for anything, but ask me for whatever you want from my money, and do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than you - meaning Aisha. He said: I had a neighbor from the Ansar, and we would take turns going down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He would go down one day and I would go down the next day, and he would bring me report of the revelation and other things, and I would bring him the same. He said: We were talking about Ghassan shod the horses to attack us. One day my friend came down and came at night, knocked on my door and called me. I went out to him and he said: A great matter has happened. I said: What is it that Ghassan has come for? He said: No, it is greater than that and more prolonged. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced his wives. I said: Hafsa has been disappointed and lost. I thought this would happen until I prayed the dawn prayer and tightened my clothes. Then I went down and entered upon Hafsa while she was crying. I said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has released you. She said: I do not know. Is he this one who is secluded in this room? So I went to a black slave of his and said: I will ask permission for Umar. The slave entered and then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I went until I came to the pulpit and there were a group of people sitting beside him, some of them crying. I sat with him for a while and then I was overcome by what I felt. So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I went out and sat by the pulpit and then I was overcome by what I felt. So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I turned away and the slave called me and said: Come in, you have been given permission. So I entered and greeted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there he was. Leaning on the sand of a mat - Imam Ahmad said: And Yaqub narrated to us in the hadith of Salih, who said: The sand of a mat - and it left an impression on his side, so I said: O Messenger of God, have you divorced your wives? He raised his head to me and said: No. So I said: God is Great. And if you had seen us, O Messenger of God, we Quraysh were a people who would overpower women, but when we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women overpowered them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day, my wife became angry with me, and I found her arguing with me, so I disapproved of her arguing with me. She said: Why do you disapprove of my arguing with you? By God, the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arguing with him, and one of them would ignore him from day to night. So I said: He who does that among you has failed and lost. Does any of you feel secure that God will not be angry with her because of the anger of the Messenger of God, and then she will be ruined? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) smiled, so I said: O Messenger of God, I entered upon Hafsa and said: Do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful or more beloved to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than you. He smiled again, so I said: Be comforted, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes. So I sat and raised my head in the house, and by God, I did not see anything in the house that would delight the eye except the preparations for his position. I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant your nation more abundantly, for He granted the Persians and Romans more abundantly, yet they did not worship God. He sat up straight and said: Are you in doubt, O son of Al-Khattab? They are a people for whom their good things have been hastened in the life of this world. I said: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month because of the intensity of his resentment towards them, until God, the Almighty, admonished him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id Al-Ansari on the authority of Ubayd ibn Hunayn on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I spent a year wanting to ask Umar ibn Al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not ask him out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj, so I went out with him. When we returned, and we were partway through the Hajj, he turned towards the arak tree because of some need he had. I stood until he finished, then I walked with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women who conspired against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. Muslim narrated it: Who are the two women about whom God the Most High said: And if they both conspire against him? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. Then he narrated the hadith in full, and some of them abbreviated it. Muslim also said: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Umar bin Yunus al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, on the authority of Samak bin al-Walid Abu Zamil, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin al-Khattab told me, he said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque, and I saw the people poking stones and saying, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had divorced his wives.” That was before the veil was ordered, so I said, I will know that today. Then he mentioned the hadith about his entering upon Aisha and Hafsa and advising them, until he said: So I entered and saw Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the threshold of the window. So I called out and said, “O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, until he said, “So I said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is difficult for you regarding the matter of women? If you have divorced them, then God is with you, and His angels, Gabriel, Michael, Abu Bakr, and I, and the believers, and I rarely spoke—and I praise God—with anything except that I hoped that it would be…’” God confirms my words, so this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you all, will give him in exchange wives better than you “And if they both back him up against him - indeed, God is his Protector and [so will] Gabriel and the righteous believers and the angels after that as support.” So I said: Have you divorced them? He said: No. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: He has not divorced his wives. And this verse was revealed: “And when there comes to them information about security or fear, they broadcast it. But if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those in authority among them, then those who can investigate it would have known about it.” So I was the one who investigated that information. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Ikrimah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Ad-Dahhak and others said: And the righteous believers means Abu Bakr and Umar. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Uthman added. Layth bin Abi Sulaym said on the authority of Mujahid: And the righteous believers means Ali bin Abi Talib. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Abi Omar told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar bin Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: A trustworthy man told me, tracing it back to Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God the Most High: And the righteous believers, he said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib. Its chain of transmission is weak and it is very objectionable. Al-Bukhari said: Umar bin Awn told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, he said: Umar said: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered in jealousy for him, so I said to them: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you. So this verse was revealed. It was mentioned before that it coincided with the Qur’an in several places: one of them in the revelation of the veil, one of them in the case of the captives of Badr, and one of them in His statement: If you took the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. So God the Most High revealed: And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Ansari told us, Humayd told us, on the authority of Anas, he said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: I was informed of something that happened between the Mothers of the Believers and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I settled them down saying: Either you refrain from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or God will replace him with wives better than you, until I came to the last of the Mothers of the Believers and she said: O Umar, is there not in the Messenger of God enough to admonish his wives so that you admonish them? So I held back and God the Almighty revealed: Perhaps if he divorces you, his Lord will give him in exchange wives better than you - Muslims, believers, obedient, repentant, worshipping God, fasting, married and virgins. This woman who turned him away from what he was doing of admonishing women was Umm Salamah as proven in Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Tabarani said: Ibrahim bin Nailah Al-Asbahani narrated to us, Ismail Al-Bajali narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement: And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, he said: Hafsah entered upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in her house while he was having intercourse with Maria. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to her: “Do not tell Aisha until I give you good report: your father will succeed Abu Bakr when I die.” So Hafsah went and informed Aisha, and Aisha said to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: Who told you this? He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me. Aisha said: I will not look at you until you forbid Maria. So he forbade her, and then God, the Most High, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid [her]? Its chain of transmission is questionable. The interpretation of these noble verses has become clear from what we have mentioned, and the meaning of His statement: Muslim women, believing women, obedient, repentant, worshipping is clear. God the Almighty says: Travelers meaning: fasting. This was said by Abu Hurairah, Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, Abu Malik, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Dahhak, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, Al-Suddi and others. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was presented in Surat Al-Bara’ah, in which the wording is: The traveler of this nation is fasting. Zayd bin Aslam and his son Abd Al-Rahman said: Travelers meaning emigrants. Abd Al-Rahman recited: Travelers, meaning emigrants. The first statement is better, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Women who are married and virgins meaning that some of them are married and some of them are virgins so that this would be more desirable to the soul, because variety expands the soul, and for this reason He said: Women who are married and virgins. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his great dictionary: Abu Bakr ibn Sadaqa told us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Marzuq told us, Abdullah ibn Umayya told us, Abdul Quddus told us, on the authority of Salih ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Buraidah, on the authority of his father, Women who are married and virgins he said: God promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this verse that He would marry him, so the married woman is Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, and the virgins are Mary, the daughter of Imran. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Mary, peace be upon her, on the authority of Suwaid bin Saeed: Muhammad bin Salih bin Umar told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Khadija passed by. He said: God sends her greetings and gives her good tidings of a house in Paradise made of hollow pearls, far from play, in which there is no toil or noise. From the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Khadijah while she was dying and said: O Khadijah, when you meet your co-wives, greet them from me. She said: “O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did you marry before me?” He said: No, but God married me to Mary, the daughter of Imran, Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Kulthum, the sister of Moses. This is also weak. Abu Ya’la said: Ibrahim ibn Arara told us, Abd al-Nur ibn Abdullah told us, Yusuf ibn Shu’ayb told us, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you know that God married me in Paradise to Mary, the daughter of Imran, Kulthum, the sister of Moses, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh? I said: Congratulations, O Messenger of God. This is also weak and was narrated as a mursal hadith on the authority of Ibn Abi Dawud.
66:5: There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of the beginning of this Surah. It has been said that it was revealed concerning Maria, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had forbidden her. Then the words of God Almighty were revealed: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ibrahim ibn Yunus ibn Muhammad told us, my father told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a female slave whom he would have intercourse with. Aisha and Hafsa kept at him until he forbade her. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? to the end of the verse. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Abu Ghassan told us, Zayd ibn Aslam told me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had intercourse with the mother of Ibrahim in the house of one of his wives. She said: O Messenger of God, in my house and on my bed? So he made her forbidden to him. She said: O Messenger of God, how do you forbid yourself what is lawful? So he swore to her by God that he would not have intercourse with her. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? Zayd ibn Aslam said: His saying, You are forbidden to me, is meaningless. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated this on the authority of his father. Ibn Jarir also said: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: He said to her: You are forbidden to me, by God I will not have intercourse with you. Sufyan al-Thawri and Ibn Ulayyah said, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath and forbade it, so he was rebuked for forbidding it and was ordered to make expiation for the oath. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and it was also narrated on the authority of Qatada and others on the authority of al-Sha’bi himself, and more than one of the early Muslims said the same, including al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatada, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Al-Awfi narrated a long story on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Jarir said: Saeed bin Yahya told us, my father told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I said to Umar bin Al-Khattab: Who are the two women? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. The conversation began with the matter of Umm Ibrahim, Maria the Copt, whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had intercourse with in Hafsa’s house during her turn. Hafsa found him and said: O Prophet of God, you have done something to me that you have not done to any of your husbands on my day, in my turn, or on my bed. He said: Are you not pleased that I forbid her and do not approach her? She said: Yes. So he forbade her and said to her: Do not mention that to anyone. She mentioned it to Aisha, and God revealed it to him, and then God revealed: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? and all the verses. It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) atoned for his oath and had intercourse with his slave girl. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb said in his Musnad: Abu Qilabah Abdul-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Umar, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hafsah: Do not tell anyone, for the mother of Ibrahim is forbidden to me. She said: Do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: By God, I will not go near her. He said: So he did not go near her until she told Aishah. He said: Then God, the Most High, revealed: God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. This is a saheeh chain of narration, and none of the authors of the six books narrated it. Al-Hafiz al-Dhiya’ al-Maqdisi chose it in his book al-Mustakhraj. Ibn Jarir also said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Hisham al-Dastawai told us: Yahya wrote to me, narrating on the authority of Ya’la bin Hakeem, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, that Ibn Abbas used to say that there is an oath that must be expiated for something forbidden. Ibn Abbas said, There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern, meaning that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his slave girl, so God, the Most High, said, “O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths.” So he expiated his oath, so the forbidden oath became an oath. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Mu’adh bin Fadalah, on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai, on the authority of Yahya, who is Ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ibn Hakeem, who is Ya’la, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the oath that must be expiated for something forbidden. Ibn Abbas said, There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern, and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Hisham al-Dastawai with it. Al-Nasa’i said: Abdullah bin Abdul Samad bin Ali informed us, Mukhallad - who is Ibn Yazid - told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man came to him and said, I have made my wife forbidden to me. He said, You have lied; she is not forbidden to you. Then he recited this verse: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? The most severe expiation for you is the freeing of a slave. Al-Nasa’i is the only one who transmitted it from this source with this wording. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Zakariya told us, Abdullah bin Raja told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade his concubine. From here, some of the jurists who said that expiation is obligatory for whoever forbids his concubine or wife, or food, drink, clothing, or any of the permissible things went, and this is the view of Imam Ahmad and a group. Al-Shafi’i said that expiation is not obligatory for anything other than the wife and the concubine if he forbade them specifically or made the prohibition general for them in one opinion. However, if he intended by the prohibition to divorce the wife or free the female slave, then it is valid for them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told me, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, Ikrimah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse, O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you? was revealed about the woman who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a strange statement, but the correct view is that it was regarding his prohibition of honey, as Al-Bukhari said regarding this verse: Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to drink honey at the home of Zaynab bint Jahsh and stay with her. Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us he entered upon should say to him: I ate maghāfir, I smell the odor of maghāfir on you. He said: No, but I used to drink honey at the home of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not do it again, and I have sworn not to tell anyone about that, “seeking to please your wives.” This is how this hadith is mentioned here with this wording. He said in the Book of Oaths and Vows: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ claimed that he heard Ubayd bin Umair say: I heard Aisha claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey at her place. Hafsa and I conspired that whichever of us the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon should say to him, “I smell the odor of maghāfir on you. I have eaten maghāfir.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon one of them, and she said that to him. He said, No, but I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not do it again. Then the verse was revealed: “O Prophet! Why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. God has already prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths. And God is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise. And when the Prophet confided a statement to one of his wives, then when she disclosed it and God disclosed it to him, he recognized part of it and turned away from part. But when he disclosed it to her, she said, ‘Who informed you of this?’ He said, ‘The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me. If you both repent to God, I will turn to You.’” God has made your hearts inclined” to Aisha and Hafsa And when the Prophet confided in some of his wives a matter to say: Rather, I drank honey. Ibrahim bin Musa said on the authority of Hisham: And I will not return to it, and I have sworn not to tell anyone about that. And thus he narrated it in the Book of Divorce with this chain of transmission and its wording is close to it, then he said: Al-Maghāfir is similar to gum that is found in the rimth and has sweetness, I forgive it with the rimth if it appears in it, its singular is maghūr and it is said maghāfir, and thus al-Jawhari said. He said that al-Maghfūr may also refer to the tenth, the thamām, the salm and the talh. He said that the rimth with a kasra is a pasture of camel pastures and it is from the sour. He said that the urfat is a tree from the tamarisk from which the maghūr exudes. Muslim narrated this hadith in the Book of Divorce in his Sahih on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hatim on the authority of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who told me on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair on the authority of Aisha, and its wording is as Al-Bukhari included it in Oaths and Vows. Then Al-Bukhari said in the Book of al-Talaq 65:Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra’ told us, Ali ibn Masahr told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved sweets and honey, and when he finished the afternoon prayer, he would go to his wives and approach one of them. He went to Hafsah bint Umar and stayed longer than he usually stayed. I became jealous and asked about that, and it was said to me that a woman from her people had given her a gift of a bowl of honey, so she gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a drink of it. I said: By God, we will find a plan for him. I said to Sawdah bint Zam’ah: He will come close to you, and when he comes close to you, say, Did you eat some saffron? He will say, No. Then say to him, What is this smell that I smell? He will say, You gave me some. Hafsa gave me a drink of honey, so say, The bees of the thorn nectar have nibbled on it, and I will tell you. You tell him, Safiyya, that. She said, "Sawda says that. By God, he had just stood at the door, and I wanted to call him as you ordered me out of fear of you. But when he came close to her, Sawda said to him, "O Messenger of God, have you eaten maghāfir? He said, No. She said, What is this odor that I smell from you? He said, Hafsa gave me a drink of honey. She said, The bees of the thorn nectar have nibbled on it." When he came to me, I said something similar. When he came to Safiyya, she said the same to him. When he came to Hafsa, she said to him, "O Messenger of God, shall I not give you some to drink? He said, I have no need of it. Sawda said, By God, we have forbidden it. I said to her, Be quiet." This is the wording of Bukhari. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Suwaid bin Saeed, on the authority of Ali bin Masaher, on the authority of Abu Kurayb, Harun bin Abdullah, and Al-Hasan bin Bishr, all three of them on the authority of Abu Usamah Hammad bin Usamah, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, and with him she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be hard pressed to have a bad odor, meaning a foul odor, and for this reason they said to him, You ate Maghafir, because its odor has something to do with it. So when he said, Rather, you drank honey, they said, His bees grazed the Arfat tree, whose gum is Maghafir, and for this reason its odor appeared in the honey they drank. Al-Jawhari said: The bees grazed the Arfat tree, meaning they ate it, and from this the bees are called Jawaris. The poet said: *They remain on the fruits of it* Al-Jaras said: Al-Jaras is a low sound. It is said: I heard the bell of a bird if you heard the sound of its beaks on something it is eating. In the hadith: They hear the bell of the bird of Paradise. Al-Asma’i said: I was in Shu’bah’s assembly. He said: They hear the crunch of the bird of Paradise with the letter sh, so I said bell. He looked at me and said: Take it from him, for he knows this better than us. The point is that this context indicates that Hafsa was the one who brought the honey. It is from Hisham bin Urwa, from his father, from his aunt Aisha. In the chain of narration of Ibn Jurayj, from Ata’, from Ubaid bin Umair, from Aisha, that Zainab bint Jahsh was the one who brought him the honey, and that Aisha and Hafsa conspired and conspired against him. And God knows best. It may be said that they both occurred, and there is nothing wrong with that, except that their being a reason for the revelation of this verse is questionable, and God knows best. What indicates that Aisha and Hafsa may God be pleased with them are the two who supported each other is the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, where he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Thawr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I was always keen to ask Umar about the two women from the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about whom God the Most High said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined, until Umar performed Hajj and I performed Hajj with him. When we were on the way, Umar turned aside and I turned aside with him with the water skin, so he defecated. Then he came to me and I poured water over his hands, and he performed ablution. I said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women from the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about whom God the Most High said: If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined, so Umar said: How strange you are, Ibn Abbas! Al-Zuhri said: By God, he disliked what he asked him about and did not conceal it. He said: They are Aisha and Hafsa. He said: Then he started to narrate the hadith. He said: We, the Quraysh, were a people who used to overpower women. When we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women used to overpower them, so our women began to learn from their women. He said: My house was in the house of Umayyah ibn Zayd in Al-Awali. He said: One day I became angry with my wife, and she spoke to me in a rude tone. I disapproved of her speaking to me, so she said: Why do you disapprove of my speaking to you? By God, the wives of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would speak to him in a rude tone, and one of them would ignore him from day to night. He said: So I went and entered upon Hafsa and said: Do you speak to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a rude tone? She said: Yes. I said: And one of you would ignore him from day to night? She said: Yes. I said: He among you who did that has failed and lost. Is any of you certain that God will not be angry with her because of the anger of His Messenger, and then she will be destroyed? Do not go back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not ask him for anything, but ask me for whatever you want from my money, and do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful and more beloved to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than you - meaning Aisha. He said: I had a neighbor from the Ansar, and we would take turns going down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He would go down one day and I would go down the next day, and he would bring me report of the revelation and other things, and I would bring him the same. He said: We were talking about Ghassan shod the horses to attack us. One day my friend came down and came at night, knocked on my door and called me. I went out to him and he said: A great matter has happened. I said: What is it that Ghassan has come for? He said: No, it is greater than that and more prolonged. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced his wives. I said: Hafsa has been disappointed and lost. I thought this would happen until I prayed the dawn prayer and tightened my clothes. Then I went down and entered upon Hafsa while she was crying. I said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has released you. She said: I do not know. Is he this one who is secluded in this room? So I went to a black slave of his and said: I will ask permission for Umar. The slave entered and then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I went until I came to the pulpit and there were a group of people sitting beside him, some of them crying. I sat with him for a while and then I was overcome by what I felt. So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I went out and sat by the pulpit and then I was overcome by what I felt. So I went to the slave and said: Ask permission for Umar. He entered and then came out to me and said: I mentioned you to him and I was silent. So I turned away and the slave called me and said: Come in, you have been given permission. So I entered and greeted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there he was. Leaning on the sand of a mat - Imam Ahmad said: And Yaqub narrated to us in the hadith of Salih, who said: The sand of a mat - and it left an impression on his side, so I said: O Messenger of God, have you divorced your wives? He raised his head to me and said: No. So I said: God is Great. And if you had seen us, O Messenger of God, we Quraysh were a people who would overpower women, but when we came to Madinah, we found a people whose women overpowered them, so our women began to learn from their women. One day, my wife became angry with me, and I found her arguing with me, so I disapproved of her arguing with me. She said: Why do you disapprove of my arguing with you? By God, the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arguing with him, and one of them would ignore him from day to night. So I said: He who does that among you has failed and lost. Does any of you feel secure that God will not be angry with her because of the anger of the Messenger of God, and then she will be ruined? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) smiled, so I said: O Messenger of God, I entered upon Hafsa and said: Do not be deceived by the fact that your neighbor is more beautiful or more beloved to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than you. He smiled again, so I said: Be comforted, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes. So I sat and raised my head in the house, and by God, I did not see anything in the house that would delight the eye except the preparations for his position. I said: O Messenger of God, pray to God to grant your nation more abundantly, for He granted the Persians and Romans more abundantly, yet they did not worship God. He sat up straight and said: Are you in doubt, O son of Al-Khattab? They are a people for whom their good things have been hastened in the life of this world. I said: Ask forgiveness for me, O Messenger of God. He had sworn that he would not enter upon them for a month because of the intensity of his resentment towards them, until God, the Almighty, admonished him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa'i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa'id Al-Ansari on the authority of Ubayd ibn Hunayn on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I spent a year wanting to ask Umar ibn Al-Khattab about a verse, but I could not ask him out of awe of him, until he went out for Hajj, so I went out with him. When we returned, and we were partway through the Hajj, he turned towards the arak tree because of some need he had. I stood until he finished, then I walked with him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two women who conspired against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. Muslim narrated it: Who are the two women about whom God the Most High said: And if they both conspire against him? He said: Aisha and Hafsa. Then he narrated the hadith in full, and some of them abbreviated it. Muslim also said: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Umar bin Yunus al-Hanafi told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, on the authority of Samak bin al-Walid Abu Zamil, Abdullah bin Abbas told me, Umar bin al-Khattab told me, he said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew from his wives, I entered the mosque, and I saw the people poking stones and saying, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had divorced his wives.” That was before the veil was ordered, so I said, I will know that today. Then he mentioned the hadith about his entering upon Aisha and Hafsa and advising them, until he said: So I entered and saw Rabah, the servant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the threshold of the window. So I called out and said, “O Rabah, ask permission for me to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Then he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, until he said, “So I said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is difficult for you regarding the matter of women? If you have divorced them, then God is with you, and His angels, Gabriel, Michael, Abu Bakr, and I, and the believers, and I rarely spoke—and I praise God—with anything except that I hoped that it would be…’” God confirms my words, so this verse was revealed, the verse of choice: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you all, will give him in exchange wives better than you “And if they both back him up against him - indeed, God is his Protector and [so will] Gabriel and the righteous believers and the angels after that as support.” So I said: Have you divorced them? He said: No. So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: He has not divorced his wives. And some of his companions were with him, among them an old man. The old man said: O Messenger of God, are the stones of Hellfire like the stones of this world? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a rock from the rocks of Hell is greater than all the mountains of the world. The old man fell unconscious, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on his heart and behold, he was alive. He called out to him and said, O old man, say ‘There is no god but God.’ He said it, and he gave him the good report of Paradise. His companions said, O Messenger of God, are you safe among us? He said, Yes. God Almighty says, That is for him who fears standing before Me and fears My threat. This is a strange mursal hadith. God the Almighty says: {Over it are angels, stern and severe} meaning their natures are stern, mercy for the disbelievers in God has been removed from their hearts. If a bird were to fly from the shoulder of one of them, it would fly for two months before reaching the other shoulder. Then they will find at the door nineteen, the width of the chest of one of them being seventy autumns. Then they will fall from one door to another for five hundred years, and they will find at each door what they found at the first door until they reach the last one. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do,” meaning it will be said to the disbelievers on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Make no excuses, for nothing will be accepted from you, and you will only be recompensed for what you used to do. You will only be recompensed today for your deeds. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Muthanna told us, Muhammad told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb: I heard An-Nu'man ibn Bashir delivering a sermon. I heard Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him say: O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance. He said: He commits a sin and does not go back on it. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Samak on the authority of An-Nu'man on the authority of Umar: He said: Sincere repentance is to repent from the sin and not return to it or not want to return to it. The chain of transmission that ends with him is more authentic, and God knows best. For this reason, the scholars said: Sincere repentance is to give up the sin in the present, regret what has been done in the past, and resolve not to do it again in the future. Then, if a person has a right to it, he should return it to him in the same way.” Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us from ‘Abd al-Karim, Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam informed me from ‘Abdullah ibn Mughaffal who said: I entered with my father upon ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and he said: “Did you hear the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘Regret is repentance?’” He said: Yes. Among them is a man having anal sex with a man, which is something that God and His Messenger have forbidden and which God and His Messenger hate. Among them is a woman having anal sex with a woman, which is something that God and His Messenger have forbidden and which God and His Messenger hate. These people have no prayer as long as they continue in this state until they repent to God with sincere repentance. Zur said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: What is sincere repentance? He said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) about that and he said: It is regret for the sins when you commit them, so you seek forgiveness from God with your regret for them in the present, then you never return to them again. So if this is the case in Islam, which is stronger than repentance, then repentance is more appropriate, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. “Perhaps” is from God. The Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him means, And He will not disgrace them with him meaning, on the Day of Resurrection. Their light will proceed before them and on their right as mentioned in Surat Al-Hadid. “They will say, ‘Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.’” Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others said: This is what the believers will say when they see the light of the hypocrites extinguished on the Day of Resurrection. Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq At-Taliqani narrated to us, Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan, from a man from Banu Kinanah, who said: I prayed behind the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in the year of the Conquest and I heard him say: O God, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said: Muhammad ibn Muqatil al-Marwazi told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that he heard Abu Dharr and Abu al-Darda’ say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will be the first to be given permission to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and the first to be given permission to raise his head. 66:8: Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of a man on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him regarding the verse: Save yourselves and your families from a Fire, meaning: educate them and teach them. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Save yourselves and your families from a Fire, meaning: obey God and avoid disobeying God, and command your families to remember God, and God will save you from the Fire. Mujahid said: Save yourselves and your families from a Fire, meaning: fear God and advise your families to fear God. Qatada said: command them to obey God and forbid them from disobeying God, and that you carry out God’s command over them, command them to do it, and help them do it. If you see something disobeying God, deter them from it and warn them against it. The jurists said: The same applies to fasting, so that it may be training for him in worship so that he may reach puberty while continuing in worship and obedience, avoiding sin and abandoning evil. And God is the Grantor of success. God the Almighty said: Its fuel is people and stones. Its fuel means its wood which is thrown into it, the corpses of the sons of Adam. And the stones It was said that what is meant by them are the idols that are worshipped, based on His Almighty saying: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hellfire. Ibn Mas`ud, Mujahid, Abu Ja`far al-Baqir, and al-Suddi said: They are stones of sulfur. Mujahid added: More putrid than a carcass. He said, Yes. God Almighty says, That is for him who fears standing before Me and fears My threat. This is a strange mursal hadith. If a bird were to fly from the shoulder of one of them, it would fly for two months before reaching the other shoulder. Then they will find at the door nineteen, the width of the chest of one of them being seventy autumns. Then they will fall from one door to another for five hundred years, and they will find at each door what they found at the first door until they reach the last one. 66:9: God Almighty says, commanding His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to wage jihad against the infidels and hypocrites, some with weapons and fighting, and others with the implementation of the prescribed punishments against them. And be harsh upon them meaning in this world. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination meaning in the Hereafter. Then God Almighty says: God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve meaning in their mixing with Muslims and their association with them, that this will not avail them at all and will not benefit them with God if faith is not present in their hearts. Then He mentioned the example and said: The wife of Noah and the wife of Lot were under two of Our righteous servants meaning two prophets and messengers who were in their company day and night, eating with them, sleeping with them, and interacting with them in the most intense company and mingling. But they betrayed them meaning in faith, they did not agree with them in faith nor did they believe them in the message. So all of that did not find anything and did not ward off any harm from them. For this reason God Almighty says: But it did not avail them at all against God meaning because of their disbelief. And it was said to the two women, Enter the Fire with those who enter. What is meant by his saying and betrayed them is not in committing an immoral act, but in religion, because the wives of the prophets are protected from committing an immoral act due to the sanctity of the prophets, as we mentioned in Surat An-Nur. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Musa ibn Abi Aisha on the authority of Sulayman ibn Qarm: I heard Ibn Abbas say about this verse, And they betrayed them, he said: They did not commit adultery. As for the betrayal of Noah’s wife, she was informing that he was crazy, and as for the betrayal of Lot’s wife, she was directing her people to his guests. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Their betrayal was that they were not of the same religion. Noah’s wife was aware of Noah’s secret, and if someone believed with Noah, she would inform the tyrants of Noah’s people. As for Lot’s wife, if Lot hosted someone, she would inform the people of Madinah about him and those who did evil. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: No prophet’s wife ever transgressed against them. Their betrayal was only in their religion. This is what Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak and others said. Some scholars have used this verse as evidence to prove the weakness of the hadith that many people attribute to God: Whoever eats with someone who has been forgiven will be forgiven. This hadith has no basis. Rather, it is narrated on the authority of some righteous people that they saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a dream and said: O Messenger of God, did you say that whoever eats with one who has been forgiven will be forgiven? He said: No, but I am saying it now.
